cases.description: A 2-link chain whose root carries delegation.extend, whose head scope and window narrow the root, signed by each issuer's active key and presented inside every window to the named audience, verifies.
A 4-link chain narrowing scope and window at every hop, each intermediate carrying delegation.extend, verifies at the maximum depth.
A chain presented by the authenticated principal named as the FINAL link's subject verifies; the presentation binding holds across the whole chain.
An empty-string presenter means no presenter was established, so the binding check is skipped just as when it is absent.
The root (an intermediate link) pair already in the seen set does NOT reject: only the final link is replay-checked, so a shared prefix can seat many distinct chains.
A different issuer's seen and revoked entry for the same grantId string as the head does not block the chain; replay and revocation key on the (issuer, grantId) pair.
A chain whose root requires a verified owner verifies when the service supplies a verified owner status.
A chain no link of which requires a verified owner verifies even when the service supplies an unverified owner status.
A chain presented at exactly the latest link's issuedAt is inside every window (inclusive lower bound).
A wrapper carrying a single link is not a chain (a one-link grant is verified by the grant verifier) and rejects on the 2-to-4 depth bound.
A wrapper carrying five links exceeds the depth cap and rejects.
A wrapper type other than network.ink.authorization_chain rejects.
An unknown top-level wrapper field is rejected by the strict schema.
An unknown field on a link is rejected by the strict delegation-link schema.
A link typed network.ink.authorization_grant is not a delegation link and rejects; a grant is never accepted as a chain link.
A parent that is not 43 base64url characters is a malformed digest and rejects on the delegation-link schema.
The root link MUST NOT carry a parent; a root that does rejects.
A non-root link MUST carry a parent; a non-root link with none rejects.
An intermediate (non-final) link whose lifetime exceeds 24 hours is over its position ceiling and rejects structurally on the signed bytes.
A final link whose lifetime exceeds 10 minutes is over its position ceiling and rejects structurally on the signed bytes.
A link with no scope entries is out of profile and rejects.
A link with a repeated scope entry rejects; scope entries must be distinct so two implementations count the same set.
A link whose expiresAt is not after issuedAt is malformed and rejects.
A verifier clock that is not a strict INK timestamp is a verifier input error consulted in pass 2 and fails closed as schema, not signature and not a window verdict.
A non-root link whose issuer does not byte-equal its parent's subject breaks continuity and rejects as chain.
A non-root link whose parent hash does not equal the digest of the link above it (a spliced parent) rejects as chain.
Editing a signed ancestor (here the root grantId) changes its canonical bytes, so the child's parent digest no longer matches and the chain rejects as chain before the signature check.
A child scope token absent from its parent is a widening and rejects the chain as attenuation.
A child whose window starts before its parent's escapes the parent window and rejects as attenuation.

A child whose issuedAt still satisfies parent.issuedAt <= child.issuedAt but whose expiresAt runs past the parent's expiresAt violates the child.expiresAt <= parent.expiresAt conjunct of window nesting; the head keeps a strictly positive window and a 10-minute lifetime so pass-1 schema does not fire first, isolating the upper-bound nesting violation as attenuation.
A 2-link chain whose root lacks delegation.extend cannot seat the re-delegation below it and rejects as attenuation; a two-link chain requires the token in the root.
A 3-link chain whose middle link drops delegation.extend cannot seat the third link, so the deeper seam rejects as attenuation even though the root seats the middle link.
A link whose signature does not verify against its resolved issuer key rejects as signature.
A retired signing key never verifies a link, the chain's fast revocation lever for a compromised delegate; the chain rejects as signature.
A revoked signing key never verifies a link; the chain rejects as signature.
A link resolved to the wrong active issuer key does not verify and rejects as signature.
A chain minted for one service presented to a different verifying service rejects on the audience check even though every signature is valid.
A chain whose final link names a different audience than the root rejects on the audience check at the mismatched link; the audience is fixed by the origin and identical on every link.
A chain presented by a principal other than its final link's subject rejects on the presentation binding.
A chain presented before the final link's issuedAt is not yet valid at that link and rejects.
A chain presented after the final link's expiresAt is expired at that link and rejects.

A chain presented at exactly the final link's expiresAt is expired: the validity window is [issuedAt, expiresAt), so now == expiresAt is outside it. This pins the exclusive upper bound, the symmetric counterpart to issued-at-lower-bound-accepts pinning the inclusive lower bound.
The final link's (issuer, grantId) pair already in the seen set is a replay and rejects.

The final link's (issuer, grantId) pair is both in the seen set and on the revocation denylist; because pass 3 reads replay before revocation under first-failure-wins, a final link that is both replayed and revoked rejects as replay, not revoked.

The final link's (issuer, grantId) pair on the revocation list rejects the chain even inside its window; an unseen head that passes the replay read still rejects on revocation and nothing is recorded.
A revoked intermediate (root) pair rejects the whole chain; every link is revocation-checked even though only the head is replay-checked.
A chain whose root requires a verified owner rejects when the owner status is unverified.
A chain whose root requires a verified owner rejects when the service supplies no owner status; absent is not verified.
A chain with a bad final signature presented to the wrong audience rejects on the signature (pass 2) ahead of the audience check (pass 3).
A chain that both widens scope and is presented after expiry rejects on attenuation (pass 1) ahead of the expiry check (pass 3).
A malformed clock with a bad signature rejects as schema: the clock is consulted at the start of pass 2, ahead of the per-link signature check.
